atoms.text: The good mind, still on the turtle’s back, begins creating a wonderful, new world. First, he creates the sun, moon and stars, so that people might have light and something by which to find their way. Then he creates the animals and plants, the oceans, rivers and seas. Finally, he creates the first people, or the Eegwahow, who look at the world and are happy. The bad mind also tries to create people, but his attempts fail, and he creates speechless apes instead.

atoms.text: Each brother wants to rule over his own creation. Neither wants to share the power of creation or the power over what is already created. The bad mind proposes a battle, the winner of which will become sole ruler of the Universe. Although the good mind does not want to share his creations, he also does not want to fight, but rather repair his relationship with his brother. The good mind tells his brother that his weakness is being whipped with cornstalks or cattails. In face of this honesty, the bad mind admits that deer antlers are his weakness, although he still insists on the battle.

atoms.text: The great battle is terrible, but it comes to pass that the good mind is victorious. The bad mind, in one last bid for power, claims control of the souls that pass from this world before sinking down into the earth and becoming the evil spirit. All the while, the good mind repairs the world, visits his people one last time, and retires from the earth forever.

What does this myth teach us?
b: It teaches us how two brothers loved each other.
++It teaches us how the world was created in the story of the Iroquois People.
